meta.scene_summary: We're building the future on a foundation of digital house of cards held together by duct tape and prayers.

cooking.headline: Turns out you can track AI models back to the GPUs they were trained on like a digital breadcrumb trail.
cooking.summary: Researchers found they can fingerprint Chinese AI models by identifying the specific export-controlled hardware used to train them. It's the ultimate 'I know what you did last summer' for global supply chain restrictions.
cooking.plain_english: Researchers have developed a method to identify the specific types of computer chips used to train artificial intelligence models by analyzing the output of those models.

cooking.headline: OpenAI fires its robotics team because the LLM finally learned how to move
cooking.summary: OpenAI realized that if your model can hallucinate a solution, you don't actually need a specialized team to build the hardware for it. It turns out the easiest way to solve robotics is to just stop building the robot and let the model pretend it's everywhere.
cooking.plain_english: OpenAI has dissolved its robotics division because it is now using its general-purpose AI models to control robotic systems instead.

cooked.headline: Microsoft's global outage is the digital equivalent of a server room fire drill during a final exam.
cooked.summary: Microsoft is currently experiencing a massive global outage that has effectively turned the internet into a very expensive paperweight. It's the perfect reminder that our entire modern infrastructure is held together by hope and a few configuration files.
cooked.plain_english: A widespread technical issue is causing global disruptions to Microsoft services and the businesses that rely on them.

cooked.headline: When the fix for the outage is not going as expected, you know it's time to just go touch some grass.
cooked.summary: Microsoft admitted that the recovery process is not going according to plan, which is engineer. speak for 'we have no idea why this is still broken.' Nothing builds confidence quite like watching the architects of the outage struggle to debug their own panic button.
cooked.plain_english: Microsoft has reported that their efforts to restore services affected by the global outage have encountered unexpected difficulties.

cooked.headline: The company that builds the world's chips just got a reminder that they aren't unhackable
cooked.summary: TSMC manufactures the silicon that powers the entire planet, yet they still couldn't stop someone from poking around their infrastructure. It's the ultimate reminder that even if you own the source of all computing power, you're still just one bad firewall config away from a bad day.
cooked.plain_english: TSMC, the world's largest semiconductor manufacturer, has reported a security breach involving unauthorized access to their systems.

cooked.headline: Claude is currently taking a mandatory mental health day
cooked.summary: The AI that usually helps us debug our code has decided to become the bug itself today. It's comforting to know that even the smartest models occasionally decide they've had enough of our prompt engineering and just go on strike.
cooked.plain_english: Anthropic's Claude AI services are currently experiencing a technical outage, preventing users from accessing the platform.

cooked.headline: Claude is currently experiencing a collective existential crisis
cooked.summary: Claude is down, which is a bit like your smartest colleague suddenly deciding to take an indefinite lunch break. It's hard to finish your sprint when the thing you're building on is literally staring at a 503 error page.
cooked.plain_english: The artificial intelligence platform Claude is currently unavailable to users due to a technical outage.

cooked.headline: Brazil's Caixa insurer accidentally made everyone's tax ID public knowledge
cooked.summary: Caixa managed to leak the data of 7.6 million customers, proving that their security strategy was apparently just 'hope nobody notices.' It's the digital equivalent of leaving your house keys in the front door lock and then going on a three. week vacation.
cooked.plain_english: A data breach at the Brazilian insurer Caixa exposed the names and tax identification numbers of 7.6 million customers.

cooked.headline: Apify had a security incident, which is the tech equivalent of leaving your keys in the ignition.
cooked.summary: Apify suffered a security incident that serves as a painful reminder that even the best web scraping tools can't scrape their way out of a data leak. It turns out that your data is only as secure as the last person who forgot to update their environment variables.
cooked.plain_english: Apify experienced a security breach that potentially exposed user data.

cooked.headline: North Korean hackers are now just using deepfakes to pass your job interview
cooked.summary: The FBI reports that hackers are using fake video calls to steal $400 million, which is the most high-stakes version of 'my camera is broken' ever recorded. It is truly peak tech progress when the most sophisticated security breach is just a really convincing Zoom background.
cooked.plain_english: The FBI has warned that North Korean hackers are using fake video calls and deepfake technology to conduct fraudulent cryptocurrency thefts.
